question: What single change in the genes can leave a person with no fingerprints at all?
answer: A mutation in SMARCAD1, traced in 2011 in a Swiss family. It hits a short version of the gene used only in skin, so carriers are otherwise healthy apart from fewer sweat glands on the hands; their fingertips are simply smooth. Border checks that demand prints gave the condition its nickname: immigration delay disease.
move: One small switch can remove a feature that seems built from countless parts.
reference: Nousbeck et al., A mutation in a skin-specific isoform of SMARCAD1 causes autosomal-dominant adermatoglyphia, American Journal of Human Genetics, 2011
